packing: Real rain shell and warm mid-layer: Girdwood averages 4.4 inches of June rain and a 53°F day.
Boat-deck layers: hat and gloves are not overkill on a six-hour fjord cruise, even in sun.
Blackout eye masks: about 18.8 hours of daylight means the sun is up past 11 p.m.
Insect repellent: Girdwood’s valley gets moderate mosquitoes from mid-June; coastal Seward is much lighter.
Binoculars: the wildlife is often distant — this is the one gear item that changes the cruise.

itinerary.labelHtml:
Day by Day

Seven nights, one base move

Seward carries the fjords, Girdwood carries the Arm, and one blank day absorbs whatever the weather does.

days.heading: Pittsburgh → Anchorage → Seward
days.feel: One long travel day, then unpack once
days.daycost: Est. $320 · rental car, fuel and meals
days.note: There is no PIT–ANC nonstop; every routing connects through Seattle, Chicago, Minneapolis or Denver. You also gain four hours going west, so a morning departure still lands with daylight to spare for the 2 hr 15 min drive to Seward.

days.heading: Exit Glacier + Seward
days.daycost: Est. $180 · groceries, meals and optional SeaLife Center

facts.label: Park fee
facts.valueHtml: None — Kenai Fjords charges no entrance fee

days.note: Join a free ranger walk at Exit Glacier, then buy groceries and let everyone adjust to the time change and the light. Do not schedule anything that has to succeed.

spots.name: Exit Glacier + Seward
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · exitglacierIG · sewardFlickr

spots.cost: Kenai Fjords National Park charges no entrance fee and the ranger-led Exit Glacier walks are free. Budget only for the Alaska SeaLife Center (about $30 adult) if you use it.
spots.climate: About 59°F high and 47°F low, and roughly 18.8 hours of daylight. June is Seward’s driest month but still logs rain on about half its days — bring a shell and stop treating the forecast as a verdict.
spots.saveHtml: Save Take the free ranger walk at 10 a.m., 2 p.m. or 4 p.m. and skip paid tours entirely on this day.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Add the SeaLife Center on a wet afternoon rather than forcing a long hike in rain.
spots.restoHtml:
• Seward Brewing Company — pizza and burgers; the reliable picky-eater pick
  • Ray’s Waterfront — burgers and chicken alongside the seafood
  • Groceries in town — Safeway on the Seward Highway for breakfasts and trail food
spots.altboxHtml:
• The lower Exit Glacier loop instead of the Harding Icefield Trail — that one is 8.2 miles with about 1,000 ft of gain per mile and holds snow into July.
  • Seward harbor and the SeaLife Center when the glacier road is socked in.

days.note: The six-hour Aialik Bay cruise is the trip’s anchor. Keep it movable within the Seward nights and spend it on the best-forecast morning.

spots.cost: Major Marine’s current six-hour Kenai Fjords cruise lists $239 adult and $119.50 child (2–11), with a deli lunch included. The 13-year-old prices as an adult, so plan roughly $840–$950 for four once tax and the per-person harbor fee land. 2027 fares are not published.
spots.climate: Dress for 45–55°F on deck even when Seward is sunny. Wind and spray make the bow far colder than the forecast; the sea itself runs about 48–51°F. This is a wildlife-and-glacier boat, never a swim.
spots.saveHtml: Save Take the six-hour Aialik Bay cruise rather than the 8.5-hour Northwestern Fjord, which the operator does not recommend under age 12.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Pay for the cruise on the settled-forecast day and treat it as the week’s one fixed anchor.
spots.restoHtml:
• Seward Brewing Company — pizza, burgers and pretzels with a bay view
  • Ray’s Waterfront — burgers and fish and chips on the harbor
  • Alaska SeaLife Center — a warm indoor backup beside the harbor
spots.altboxHtml:
• The four-hour Resurrection Bay cruise if six hours on the water reads as too long for the 8-year-old.
  • Alaska SeaLife Center when the boat cancels for weather — puffins and otters at eye level, indoors.

days.heading: Seward → Turnagain Arm → Girdwood
days.daycost: Est. $260 · wildlife center, fuel and meals
days.note: The only base move of the week. Break it with the Alaska Wildlife Conservation Center and the Turnagain Arm pullouts rather than driving it straight through.

spots.cost: Alaska Wildlife Conservation Center lists $30 adult and $26 youth (4–12) — about $116 for four. The Portage Glacier cruise runs roughly $49–$69 per person. The Whittier tunnel toll is $13 per car round-trip and is only needed if you actually cross to Whittier.
spots.climate: Cooler and wetter than Seward — Girdwood averages about 53°F and 4.4 inches of June rain. The Arm makes its own weather; the drive is worth doing even under cloud.
spots.saveHtml: Save The Arm’s pullouts — Beluga Point, Bird Point — cost nothing and carry the scenery on their own.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge The wildlife center is the trip’s most reliable bear-and-moose sighting, and it is worth the money precisely because it is not left to luck.
spots.restoHtml:
• Chair 5 — pizza and burgers made to order; the best picky-eater option in Girdwood
  • Jack Sprat — a real kids’ menu at the base of the tram
  • Hotel Alyeska — in-house options when nobody wants to drive again
spots.altboxHtml:
• The bore tide at Beluga Point — it runs about 2 hr 15 min after Anchorage low tide, so it is a tide-table plan, not a whim.
  • Byron Glacier’s short trail if the Portage cruise is full or cancelled.

days.heading: Alyeska tram + Girdwood
days.note: Ride the tram for the Turnagain Arm view, walk the ridge if the weather allows, and keep the afternoon free. The hotel pool is capped at one reserved hour a day, so book it early if the kids want it.

days.heading: Portage Glacier + Byron
days.feel: Icebergs and a short forest trail
days.note: Portage Lake still carries ice in June. The m/v Ptarmigan runs five daily departures; Byron Glacier’s short trail is the free alternative if it is booked out.

days.heading: Weather-reset day
days.note: Keep this blank until the forecast settles. It can rescue the cruise, become an Anchorage day, a Virgin Creek Falls walk, laundry, or simply nothing at all.

days.heading: Girdwood → Anchorage → Pittsburgh
days.note: Girdwood to ANC is about 45 minutes. You lose the four hours back, so an afternoon departure becomes a next-day arrival — check what the return red-eye actually costs the family before booking it.

/* Tooltip */
/* Base styles for the element that has a tooltip */
.leaflet-tooltip {
	position: absolute;
	padding: 6px;
	background-color: #fff;
	border: 1px solid #fff;
	border-radius: 3px;
	color: #222;

.leaflet-tooltip-right:before {

	}

}
.leaflet-tooltip-top {

}
.leaflet-tooltip-bottom:before,
.leaflet-tooltip-top:before {

Where You Will Go

One highway, two bases

Everything sits on the Seward Highway between Anchorage and Resurrection Bay. The fjords are reachable only by boat.

Getting to Alaska

Every routing connects

There is no PIT–ANC nonstop. Plan a one-stop day of roughly 9–10 hours each way and treat the four-hour time change as part of the itinerary.

Preferred outbound

DateSat Jun 12
RoutePIT → SEA/ORD/MSP/DEN → ANC
Family air band$2,000–$3,000 with bags/seats
Time changeGain 4 hours westbound
A morning departure lands with hours of daylight left — Alaska in June makes an evening arrival drive genuinely easy.

Return

DateSat Jun 19
Drive bufferGirdwood → ANC · about 45 min
Time changeLose 4 hours eastbound
An afternoon ANC departure arrives in Pittsburgh the next day. Price that red-eye honestly before assuming it is the cheap option.

Getting Around

One rental car for the whole week

The Seward Highway is the trip. A car beats the train here because the wildlife center, the Arm pullouts and Portage are all roadside stops the train passes by.

Rental car

Pickup / returnANC
Planning band$700–$1,100 all-in
ANC → SewardAbout 2 hr 15 min
Seward → GirdwoodAbout 1 hr 45 min
June is peak; Alaska rental rates surge harder than the lower 48. Book early — this line moves more than airfare does.

The train alternative

ServiceAlaska Railroad Coastal Classic
Current fare$133 adult / $67 child one-way
DurationAbout 4 hours
Beautiful, and about $800 round-trip for four — but it strands you without a car in Seward and skips Portage entirely. Take it only if nobody wants to drive.

What Could Change

Weather, wildlife and one boat

The plan is simple, but a single cancelled cruise removes the headline. Everything here is about protecting that one day.

Act now

The cruise is a single point of failure

Weather cancels Kenai Fjords sailings. Book it early in the Seward nights so a cancellation still has a spare day to land on.

Watch

Bears are real, not decorative

June brings mothers with cubs and the start of the salmon run. Stick to ranger-led walks and well-travelled trails; skip backcountry hiking as a family.

Watch

Alyeska pool policy

Current policy caps the pool at one reserved hour per day. Reconfirm — it is the only warm water on the trip.

Good

Daylight is a safety margin

About 18.8 hours of it means a blown morning is fully recoverable in the evening.

Why These Dates

Juneteenth saves a PTO day

Saturday to Saturday, four PTO days, and home well before the family’s Jun 24–26 Pittsburgh commitment.

Preferred

Jun 12–19

Hotel nights7
PTO days4
Daylight~18.8 hr

Later June for warmer water

Sea temp gainNegligible
MosquitoesWorse mid-June onward
Verdict: early-to-mid June is the right window — it is Seward’s driest month, the light is near its maximum, and the mosquitoes have not yet peaked. Waiting will not warm the water.

Planning Budget

The most expensive short escape here

Alaska does not come in cheap. Airfare and Girdwood lodging are the two lines that decide whether this lands near $9k or near $12.6k.

Keep it near the floor

  • Book airfare early — $500/person and $750/person are both realistic.
  • Take the six-hour cruise, not the 8.5-hour Northwestern Fjord.
  • Use the free ranger walks and the Arm pullouts; they carry the scenery.
  • A Girdwood condo with a kitchen would cut both lodging and food — at the cost of Alyeska’s pool.

Worth paying for

  • The Kenai Fjords cruise. It is the trip.
  • The wildlife center — guaranteed bears and moose beat hoping.
  • A Seward room by the cruise dock.

Airfare and the boat first

Everything else in Southcentral Alaska has slack. These two do not.

  5. Reconfirm the Alyeska pool policy· only warm water on the trip

Family Fit

Wildlife carries the 8-year-old

The cruise and the wildlife center do the heavy lifting; nothing here demands a hard hike.

For the 13-year-old

genuinely big country

  • Calving glaciers and breaching humpbacks are not kid programming.
  • The tram ridge and Harding Icefield trail offer real effort if wanted.
  • Note: prices as an adult on the cruise.

For the 8-year-old

short wins, no forced miles

  • Six hours on a boat is the longest ask all week.
  • Guaranteed bears and moose at the wildlife center.
  • The free ranger walk reaches a glacier without a climb.

For picky eaters

pizza and burgers exist

  • Chair 5 in Girdwood makes pizza and burgers to order.
  • Seward Brewing covers pizza and burgers in town.
  • Grizzly’s Pizza sits inside the Anchorage terminal for travel days.

Trip Balance

Nature-dominant, and unapologetic about it

This is the least balanced trip on the board by design. There is almost no swimming and the towns are small.
